message: Provenance correction: the BLS citation now points to its dated November 3 archive, and the public evidence includes the cited sector and establishment-size details. Figures and interpretation are unchanged from the 12:11 PM ET edition.

data.headline: IWM: distinguish small workplaces from listed small caps.
data.summary: BLS reports a lower layoffs-and-discharges rate at workplaces with one to nine employees, alongside little change in several other measures for that size class. That observation is relevant context but is not a Russell 2000 company sample. Small-cap finance and positioning remain separate parts of the assessment.

bull.text: For establishments with 1–9 employees, the layoffs-and-discharges rate decreased in September. BLS said openings, hires, quits and total-separation rates showed little or no change. Establishment size is not an equity-index classification.

bear.text: Economy-wide quits increased to 3.4 million. This may matter for staffing conditions, but the survey does not provide Russell 2000 refinancing costs, margins or a measured price response.

watch.text: October 27 Russell E-mini futures asset managers were net long 19,602 contracts and leveraged funds net short 48,081. The earlier October 20 balances were net long 30,960 and net short 53,035, respectively; this is category positioning rather than IWM subscriptions.

limitations: BLS observations describe September and were released November 3 at 10:00 AM ET; they are survey estimates subject to revision. No economist consensus or release-day price reaction was collected.
CFTC observations are October 27 futures-only category positions, released with a lag. Related futures are not ETF holdings, live fund flows or named-investor intent.
Current price levels, option chains, gamma, social sentiment and dark-pool direction are not independently measured here. Hosted TradingView displays remain separate.
This AI-assisted contextual report has no validated directional forecast or conviction score.
